projects.name: AI Surface Defect Classification & Explainability
projects.role: Data pipeline, model training, explainability analysis and demo interface — independently delivered
projects.summary: A reproducible vision-classification build on an industrial surface-defect problem: constructed a data pipeline from a public industrial dataset, compared CNN and Transformer transfer learning under an identical protocol, validated model evidence against human annotations using Grad-CAM, and packaged the result into a live inference demo. The goal was to test whether "accurate is not enough — a line AI must explain its call" is workable in practice.
highlights: Dataset: NEU-DET steel surface defect benchmark (shop-floor collected, 1,770 images x 6 classes: crazing, inclusion, patches, pitted surface, rolled-in scale, scratches), stratified train/val/test split with a fixed seed (1,236/264/270), verified leak-free.
Models: ResNet18 (CNN) and ViT-B/16 (Transformer), both ImageNet-pretrained transfer learning; both reached 100% accuracy and macro-F1 1.00 on a 270-image held-out test set.
Explainability: Grad-CAM heatmaps overlaid against ground-truth boxes, 12/12 aligned; observed CNN heatmaps concentrating on the defect body while ViT attention spread wider.
Engineering: NVIDIA RTX 5060 (Blackwell) + PyTorch CUDA 12.8 + bf16 mixed precision; fully scripted and reproducible.
Deliverables: data pipeline, training/evaluation scripts, confusion matrix and classification report, Grad-CAM comparison, Gradio inference demo.

details.title: Problem framing and data pipeline
details.text: Six steel surface defect classes were used as the classification target; Pascal VOC annotations were parsed into class labels with a fixed-seed stratified split ensuring disjoint train/val/test sets, plus sample and bounding-box references as a baseline for later explainability comparison.

details.title: Model comparison and architecture observation
details.text: CNN and Transformer were compared under an identical split and training protocol; both reached 100% on the held-out set, indicating that for well-defined industrial defect classification, image features and pretrained representations are already sufficient. The real difference appeared in explainability — CNN heatmaps concentrate on the defect body while ViT attention spreads wider, reflecting how architecture affects how readable a model's evidence is, and what a line-selection decision must weigh beyond accuracy.

details.title: Explainability and scope boundary
details.text: Grad-CAM was used to visualize model evidence against human annotations, confirming that attended regions align with defect locations — a key requirement for line AI, where verdicts must be traceable for QA, process and customers, not just a score. Scope note: this is offline validation on a public dataset, not a production deployment; the dataset is limited in scale and scenario, and 100% accuracy reflects benchmark characteristics rather than mass-production performance.

projects.source: Personal development record (GitHub: ai-aoi) | NEU-DET public industrial surface-defect dataset

projects.name: AI Process & Engineering Parameter Optimization
projects.role: Participated in engineering pull-force prediction and supported manufacturing AI applications through plant management.
projects.summary: Translated manufacturing and design problems into measurable parameters, prediction targets and validation workflows. Studied key pressing, paint fixtures, pogo-pin force, keycap pull force and laser-engraving parameter optimization.
highlights: Pull-force prediction: the presentation explicitly lists Jason Hung as a participant. Material, opening dimensions and force data were explored to support design decisions and reduce trial and error.

Cross-functional case: the key-pressing project reported an offline experimental metric increasing from 200 to 1,113 pcs per operation. This is a team-reported result for a specific operation, not a whole-line capacity increase.
Implementation approach: connect shop-floor problems, data preparation, modeling, parameter recommendations and offline validation, distinguishing validated results from cost estimates.

details.title: Research Question & Method
details.text: The keycap pull-force project addressed hook-opening dimensions that relied on experience and tooling trials. It used material and historical force data to explore dimension prediction and parameter recommendations. The presentation records 20 modeling samples and 3 additional test samples: preliminary validation requiring more data across specifications and operating conditions.

details.title: Manufacturing Validation
details.text: The key-pressing case combined cylinder pressure, ejection time, pressing time and rubber hardness. Following model recommendations and offline testing, the team reported a metric increase from 200 to 1,113 pcs per operation. The original unit and limited scope are retained.

details.title: Benefits & Research Limitations
details.text: The pull-force project estimated RMB 104,800 per year across tooling modification, experimental labor and new-hire training. This is a scenario estimate, not realized savings, and is not added to the RMB 2M+ annual result in the resume. Further work includes tolerance recommendations, larger samples and continued offline validation.

projects.source: AI Project Optimization Summary, slides 20, 22, 62, 66–67, 71, 74 and 79–80. Named participation applies to the pull-force project; other cases summarize team reports.

projects.name: E-Vehicle Controller Embedded Development
projects.summary: Building on 10+ years of embedded development experience, ongoing firmware and tooling development for an e-bike controller (three-phase BLDC motor control): motor control algorithms, migration of production-proven protection logic, communication protocol design, Windows tuning tools and AI-assisted diagnostics over logged operating data.

details.title: Motor Control & Firmware
details.text: Re-implemented production-proven control logic on a modern dual-core MCU with integrated CAN/BLE: three-phase BLDC commutation and SVPWM sinusoidal control, overcurrent / undervoltage / stall protection, and firmware-level electromagnetic braking (E-ABS) with regenerative energy recovery and safety management.

details.title: Protocols & Toolchain
details.text: Designed serial communication protocols and debug frames (controller–display–BMS) and built a Windows tuning tool covering parameter read/write, Hall calibration, live charts and diagnostic export, supporting motor matching and production calibration.

details.title: AI Applications
details.text: Exported operating data (current, speed, voltage, load state) as structured diagnostic packages; explored LLM-assisted fault diagnosis and motor-parameter self-learning as a bridge to IoT services and after-sales applications.

projects.name: E-Vehicle Battery Management System (BMS) Development
projects.summary: End-to-end design of a 36V (10S) lithium battery management system: analog front-end (AFE) selection, host MCU and CAN architecture, safety-gated regenerative braking with advance negotiation, and online terminal contact-resistance monitoring — with full schematic, pin-level wiring table and CAN protocol draft delivered.

details.title: Architecture & Hardware
details.text: BQ76930 AFE + STM32F103 (built-in bxCAN) + CAN transceiver: 10S cell sampling and balancing, charge/discharge MOS power stage, 42V-to-5V buck with integrated Bluetooth speaker; full schematic and pin-level connection table delivered.

details.title: Protocol & Regen Safety
details.text: Mapped the legacy RS232 battery protocol onto J1939-style CAN frames for controller integration; regenerative braking gated by a two-layer mechanism (safety admission + advance no-regen negotiation) with multi-level SOC/temperature/current thresholds, protecting both battery and controller lifespan across a two-phase rollout plan.

details.title: Reliability & Differentiating Features
details.text: Self-developed B+/P+ dual-point online contact-resistance monitoring that estimates power-loop contact resistance in real time with tiered alerts, catching outdoor plug corrosion and fretting degradation early; plus an anthropomorphic voice-prompt feature (battery / health / connection status, language and voice switchable via app).

projects.name: Industrial Edge Gateway (Hardware + Software + AI)
projects.summary: Born from a universal manufacturing pain point: legacy equipment (RS-232 proprietary-protocol meters, old PLCs) holds data that cannot be extracted, and vendor-based integration is costly with no guarantee of success. The direction of this project is a hardware-software-AI system that turns proprietary protocol integration from custom development into configuration — an in-house low-cost edge node board for physical access, a JSON protocol-description engine that parses any proprietary frame format with zero code changes, and AI that generates protocol profiles and alarm rules from packet samples and plain-language descriptions, connecting old machines to data platforms quickly and affordably.

details.title: Edge Node Hardware
details.text: In-house DIN-rail node board: ESP32-S3 host + CH438 multi-UART expansion, isolated RS-232 x4 / RS-485 x2 / CAN x1, 9-36V industrial input with surge protection, Ethernet/WiFi uplink to MQTT.

details.title: JSON Protocol Engine
details.text: No hard-coded protocols: frame header/length/checksum/field layout lives in one JSON profile, parsed by a streaming engine tolerant of arbitrary byte splits and bad frames — adding a device is a configuration change, not a code change; a local rule engine (debounced thresholds, deadband filtering) handles edge computing.

details.title: AI-Assisted Integration
details.text: AI generates protocol profiles and rules from packet captures and plain-language descriptions for human review, cutting protocol reverse-engineering from days to minutes; the run-time direction adds lightweight on-node anomaly detection.

projects.name: Smart Door Lock Product Definition & Selection (NPI)
projects.role: Requirement definition, solution selection and cost engineering — independently delivered (design phase, ongoing)
projects.summary: Targeting one hardware platform shared across three scenarios — home, apartment and small B&B — redefined the requirements for a full-featured smart door lock (WiFi / Bluetooth / key card / PIN / fingerprint / doorbell / App / smart-home ecosystem), and completed the ecosystem route decision, main-MCU and peripheral selection, the unit cost structure and mass-production cost engineering, plus the architecture plan for a hotel-grade complete system (lock + gateway + card encoder + management software); on top of existing Bluetooth lock assets, planned auto double-locking and tamper warning as differentiating features.

details.title: Requirement redefinition and solution selection
details.text: Reframed "WiFi home integration" as Matter compliance (Apple / Google / Amazon / SmartThings) and established BLE as a mandatory commissioning channel rather than an option. After comparing in-house development, commercial module and hybrid routes, settled on a two-tier architecture: ESP32-C6 (WiFi 6 + BLE 5.3 + 802.15.4, Matter-native) as the main MCU, with a low-power co-processor (450 nA deep sleep) handling always-on standby and touch wake. Completed unified peripheral selection (card reader, semiconductor fingerprint, 6068 standard lock body, voice prompt, isolated motor drive). Hardware reserves Aliro (phone-wallet tap-to-unlock) capability, settled once and rolled out in software phases.

details.title: Cost engineering and three-scenario configuration
details.text: Built the unit cost structure, breaking it into eight cost blocks and identifying the credential layer (card reader, fingerprint and other identity factors) as the dominant cost item and negotiation focus, then used that to set tiered cost targets and an RFQ strategy for volume production. The key architectural decision is one board, many configurations — home / apartment / B&B run on direct WiFi with no gateway required, while hotels use BLE reporting plus a PoE gateway for centralized management (one gateway serving multiple doors); hardware differences reduce to lock-body grade, door sensor and enclosure material, so all three scenarios share one PCB and one firmware.

details.title: Hotel-grade system and differentiating features
details.text: Planned the complete hotel-grade system — lock, gateway, card encoder, housekeeping management software and installation/delivery as one architecture — with optimized gateway coverage and a lightweight system as the source of cost advantage, supported by an RFQ list and a technical risk register (including key-component supply and price locking). Also planned auto double-locking with tamper warning: scheduled or sensed escalation to double lock with tiered response (physical hardening before alarm), four sensing paths with two-path cross-validation to cut false alarms, mapped to Matter's native lock states and DoorForcedOpen alarm code.

projects.source: Personal development record (smart lock selection plan v1.0 / feature addendum v1.1) | Reused existing Bluetooth lock project assets
